23011-eatin-crow-and-the-best-man-in-gar.title: Eatin Crow And The Best Man In Garotte
23011-eatin-crow-and-the-best-man-in-gar.creator: Frank Harris
23011-eatin-crow-and-the-best-man-in-gar.description: A book by Frank Harris. At length in answer to Bent's continued grumbling, Muirhead said pleasantly: “'Tain't so bad as that in Garotte, is it? This bar don't look like poverty, and if I set up drinks for the crowd, it's because I'm glad to be in this camp.”

35704-wonder-stories-the-best-myths-for-.title: Wonder Stories The Best Myths For Boys And Girls
35704-wonder-stories-the-best-myths-for-.creator: Unknown
35704-wonder-stories-the-best-myths-for-.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Long ago, when our earth was more than two thousand years younger, there was a wonderful place called Mount Olympus at the top of the world that the ancients could see quite clearly with the eyes of hope and faith. It did not matter that the Greek and Roman people had never set foot on this mountain in the clouds.

The duty of taking the most effective precautions to this end is one that naturally falls to the Legislature, especially under a Government professing to regard social questions as of paramount importance.

arxiv-2109-13396.title: Bridge Data: Boosting Generalization of Robotic Skills with Cross-Domain Datasets
arxiv-2109-13396.creator: Frederik Ebert*, Yanlai Yang*, Karl Schmeckpeper, Bernadette Bucher, Georgios Georgakis, Kostas Daniilidis, Chelsea Finn, Sergey Levine
arxiv-2109-13396.description: Abstract Robot learning holds the promise of learning policies that generalize broadly. However, such generalization requires sufficiently diverse datasets of the task of interest, which can be prohibitively expensive to collect. In other fields, such as computer vision, it is common to utilize shared, reusable datasets, such as ImageNet, to overcome this challenge, but this has proven difficult in robotics.

arxiv-2110-13134.title: Constructing k-local parent Lindbladians for matrix product density operators
arxiv-2110-13134.creator: Dmytro Bondarenko
arxiv-2110-13134.description: Abstract Matrix product density operators (MPDOs) are an important class of states with interesting properties. Consequently, it is important to understand how to prepare these states experimentally. One possible way to do this is to design an open system that evolves only towards desired states. A Markovian evolution of a quantum mechanical system can be generally described by a Lindbladian.

arxiv-2201-08261.title: Optimization of a Reed-Solomon code-based protocol against blockchain data availability attacks
arxiv-2201-08261.creator: Dipartimento di Ingegneria dell’Informazione Università Politecnica delle Marche, Ancona (60131), Italy email:{p.santini, g.rafaiani, m.battaglioni, f.chiaraluce, m.baldi}@univpm.it
arxiv-2201-08261.description: Abstract ASBK (named after the authors’ initials) is a recent blockchain protocol tackling data availability attacks against light nodes, employing two-dimensional Reed-Solomon codes to encode the list of transactions and a random sampling phase where adversaries are forced to reveal information.

arxiv-2205-12068.title: Construction and analysis of the quadratic finite volume methods on tetrahedral meshes Thanks: This work is partially supported by the National Science Foundation of China (No.12071177), and the Science Challenge Project (No. TZ2016002).
arxiv-2205-12068.creator: Peng Yang, Xiang Wang, Yonghai Li
arxiv-2205-12068.description: Abstract . A family of quadratic finite volume method (FVM) schemes are constructed and analyzed over tetrahedral meshes. In order to prove stability and error estimate, we propose the minimum V-angle condition on tetrahedral meshes, and the surface and volume orthogonal conditions on dual meshes.

arxiv-2211-10797.title: An Empirical Study On Contrastive Search And Contrastive Decoding For Open-ended Text Generation
arxiv-2211-10797.creator: Yixuan Su, Jialu Xu
arxiv-2211-10797.description: Abstract In the study, we empirically compare the two recently proposed decoding methods, i.e. Contrastive Search (CS) and Contrastive Decoding (CD), for open-ended text generation. The automatic evaluation results suggest that, while CS performs worse than CD on the MAUVE metric, it substantially surpasses CD on the diversity and coherence metrics.

arxiv-2303-03069.title: Hidden scale invariance in the Gay-Berne model. II. Smectic B phase
arxiv-2303-03069.creator: Saeed Mehri, Jeppe C. Dyre, Trond S. Ingebrigtsen
arxiv-2303-03069.description: Abstract This paper complements a previous study of the isotropic and nematic phases of the Gay-Berne liquid-crystal model [Mehri et al ., Phys. Rev. E 105 , 064703 (2022)] with a study of its smectic B phase found at high density and low temperatures.

arxiv-2306-05930.title: Positivity Certificates for Linear Recurrences
arxiv-2306-05930.creator: Alaa Ibrahim and Bruno Salvy
arxiv-2306-05930.description: Abstract . We consider linear recurrences with polynomial coefficients of Poincaré type and with a unique simple dominant eigenvalue. We give an algorithm that proves or disproves positivity of solutions provided the initial conditions satisfy a precisely defined genericity condition. For positive sequences, the algorithm produces a certificate of positivity that is a data-structure for a proof by induction.

arxiv-2401-17353.title: Theory of a Strange Metal in a Quantum Superconductor to Metal Transition
arxiv-2401-17353.creator: Jaewon Kim, Erez Berg, Ehud Altman
arxiv-2401-17353.description: Abstract Recent experiments with nanopatterned thin films revealed an unusual quantum superconductor to metal phase transition (QSMT) with a linear in temperature resistivity. In contrast, most known examples of such transitions and standard theoretical considerations predict a temperature-independent sheet resistance of order R Q = ℏ e 2 R_{Q}=\frac{\hbar}{e^{2}} .

arxiv-2503-04923.title: Splicing skew shaped positroids
arxiv-2503-04923.creator: Eugene Gorsky, Soyeon Kim, Tonie Scroggin, José Simental
arxiv-2503-04923.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Eugene Gorsky, Soyeon Kim, Tonie Scroggin, José Simental. Skew shaped positroids (or skew shaped positroid varieties) are certain Richardson varieties in the flag variety that admit a realization as explicit subvarieties of the Grassmannian Gr ⁡ ( k , n ) \mathrm{Gr}(k,n) . They are parametrized by a pair of Young diagrams μ ⊆ λ \mu\subseteq\lambda fitting inside a k × ( n − k ) k\times(n-k) -rectangle.

arxiv-2506-11704.title: Isometric-Universal Graphs for Trees
arxiv-2506-11704.creator: Edgar Baucher, François Dross, Cyril Gavoille
arxiv-2506-11704.description: Abstract We consider the problem of finding the smallest graph that contains two input trees each with at most n n vertices preserving their distances. In other words, we look for an isometric-universal graph with the minimum number of vertices for two given trees.

arxiv-2507-13879.title: Magnetic monopoles with an internal degree of freedom
arxiv-2507-13879.creator: Petr Beneš, Filip Blaschke
arxiv-2507-13879.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Petr Beneš, Filip Blaschke. We consider a class of spontaneously broken S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) SU(2)_{\mathrm{}} gauge theories with adjoint scalar and look for exact magnetic monopole solutions in the Bogomol’nyi–Prasad–Sommerfield (BPS) limit. We find that some of the resulting solutions exhibit a new internal degree of freedom (a moduli space parameter) that controls the energy density profile of the monopole while keeping the total energy (mass) constant.

arxiv-2509-01001.title: Generalized promotion time cure model: A new modeling framework to identify cell-type-specific genes and improve survival prognosis
arxiv-2509-01001.creator: Zhi Zhao, Fatih Kizilaslan, Shixiong Wang, Manuela Zucknick
arxiv-2509-01001.description: Abstract Single-cell technologies provide an unprecedented opportunity for dissecting the interplay between the cancer cells and the associated tumor microenvironment, and the produced high-dimensional omics data should also augment existing survival modeling approaches for identifying tumor cell type-specific genes predictive of cancer patient survival.

arxiv-2509-11992.title: The List-distinguishing chromatic number of graphs containing only small complete bigraphs
arxiv-2509-11992.creator: Amitayu Banerjee
arxiv-2509-11992.description: Abstract . Let G G be a simple finite graph with maximum degree Δ ⁡ ( G ) \Delta(G) . The distinguishing chromatic number χ D ​ ( G ) \chi_{D}(G) of G G is the minimum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of G G that is preserved only by the identity automorphism.

arxiv-2512-17802.title: Systematic search of laser and phase modulation noise coupling in heterodyne interferometry
arxiv-2512-17802.creator: Kohei Yamamoto, Olaf Hartwig, Lennart Wissel, Holly Leopardi, Kenji Numata, Ryan Derosa
arxiv-2512-17802.description: Abstract Heterodyne interferometry for precision science often comes with an optical phase modulation, for example, for intersatellite clock noise transfer for gravitational wave (GW) detectors in space, exemplified by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). The phase modulation potentially causes various noise couplings to the final phase extraction of heterodyne beatnotes by a phasemeter.

arxiv-2602-07201.title: Measurement-Based Preparation of Higher-Dimensional AKLT States and Their Quantum Computational Power
arxiv-2602-07201.creator: Wenhan Guo, Mikhail Litvinov, Tzu-Chieh Wei, Abid Khan, Kevin C. Smith
arxiv-2602-07201.description: Abstract We investigate a constant-time, fusion measurement-based scheme to create AKLT states beyond one dimension. We show that it is possible to prepare such states on a given graph up to random spin-1 ‘decorations’, each corresponding to a probabilistic insertion of a vertex along an edge.

arxiv-2606-16045.creator: Vincent Cohen-Addad, Sasidhar Kunapuli, Vahab Mirrokni, Mahdi Nikdan, David P. Woodruff, Samson Zhou

britannica-1911-agapetus-pope.title: Agapetus (pope) (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-agapetus-pope.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-agapetus-pope.description: Article 'Agapetus (pope)' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 1), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Agapetus I., pope from 536 to 536. He was an enlightened pontiff and collaborated with Cassiodorus in founding at Rome a library of ecclesiastical authors. King Theodahad sent him on an embassy to Constantinople, where he died, after having deposed Anthimus, the monophysite bishop of that town, and ordained Menas his successor.

pmc-11394638.title: Exploring the Role of the Gut Microbiota in Modulating Colorectal Cancer Immunity
pmc-11394638.creator: Nikolay K Shakhpazyan, Liudmila M Mikhaleva, Arkady L Bedzhanyan, Zarina V Gioeva, Alexander I Mikhalev, Konstantin Y Midiber, Valentina V Pechnikova, Andrey E Biryukov, Li Yang, Claudia D Andl
pmc-11394638.description: The gut microbiota plays an essential role in maintaining immune homeostasis and influencing the immune landscape within the tumor microenvironment. This review aims to elucidate the interactions between gut microbiota and tumor immune dynamics, with a focus on colorectal cancer (CRC).

pmc-11456431.title: Potentially suitable geographical area for Colletotrichum acutatum under current and future climatic scenarios based on optimized MaxEnt model
pmc-11456431.creator: Chun Fu, Yaqin Peng, Fengrong Yang, Zhipeng He, Habib Ali, Danping Xu
pmc-11456431.description: Global climate warming has led to changes in the suitable habitats for fungi. Colletotrichum acutatum, a common fungus causing anthracnose disease, is widely distributed in southern China. Currently, research on the relationship between C. acutatum and environmental warming was limited. In this study, MaxEnt and ArcGIS software were used to predict the suitable habitats of C.

pmc-12522285.title: Towards a better understanding of brief lifestyle interventions in noncommunicable diseases: a concept analysis
pmc-12522285.creator: Binglu Wang, Quan Shen, Meili Xiao, Shujuan Zhu, Jia Qu, ENuo Peng, Jun Lei
pmc-12522285.description: Background Brief lifestyle interventions targeting diet and physical activity play a critical role in the prevention and management of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs). However, healthcare providers often report feeling inadequately prepared to deliver such interventions, as there is limited guidance available to inform their practice.ObjectiveTo define and describe the concept of “brief lifestyle intervention” within the context of NCDs.DesignA concept analysis.

pmc-12547437.title: Temporal variation in microplastic abundance in sediment, fish and shrimp: a case study in the Thames Estuary, UK
pmc-12547437.creator: Alexandra Rachael McGoran, Paul Frederick Clark, Brian Smith, David Morritt
pmc-12547437.description: Microplastics are abundant in marine and terrestrial habitats, with rivers transporting particles to the sea. The River Thames catchment, UK, encompasses 15 million residents and many pollution sources. Temporal trends in microplastic abundance are sparse, with ad hoc studies in the estuary demonstrating great variability in concentrations.

pmc-12585480.title: Pipe(line) dreams for MicroED/3DED sample preparation
pmc-12585480.creator: Katherine A Spoth, Gabrielle R Budziszewski, M Elizabeth Snell, Miranda L Lynch, Devrim Acehan, Sarah EJ Bowman
pmc-12585480.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Microcrystal electron diffraction (MicroED) has experienced incredible growth as a powerful technique for structure determination. Similar to all diffraction-based structural methods for biomolecules, a bottleneck in using MicroED to solve structures is the need to generate crystals. The challenge of making crystals is slightly different for MicroED, since the crystals required are in the submicron size range, smaller than the wavelength of visible light and therefore difficult to detect.

pmc-12717030.title: Assessing the Impact of Whole Genome Duplication on Gene Expression and Regulation During Arachnid Development
pmc-12717030.creator: Madeleine E Aase-Remedios, Daniel J Leite, Ralf Janssen, Alistair P McGregor
pmc-12717030.description: Whole genome duplication (WGD) generates a new genetic material that can contribute to the evolution of developmental processes and phenotypic diversification. A WGD occurred in an ancestor of arachnopulmonates (spiders, scorpions, and their relatives), which provides an important independent comparison to WGDs in other animal lineages.

pmc-13095555.title: A comparative analysis of safety and short-term efficacy between open and laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy utilizing different drainage techniques
pmc-13095555.creator: Changjun Liu, Chen Zou, Pengxiang Tang, Hanyu Liu, Weinan Liu, Lian Shen, Kang Chen, Wei Cheng, Bingzhang Tian, Shuo Qi, Bowen Xie
pmc-13095555.description: PurposeTo evaluate the safety profiles of open pancreaticoduodenectomy (OPD) and laparoscopic pancreaticoduodenectomy (LPD), and to analyze the respective advantages and disadvantages of various internal and external drainage techniques.MethodsAll 260 patients successfully underwent laparoscopic or open PD. They were divided into laparoscopy and laparotomy groups by surgical approach, and into internal and external drainage groups by drainage method.

pmc-13535158.title: Endodontic Microsurgery as a Primary Treatment for Pulp Canal Obliteration With Apical Periodontitis: Case Reports
pmc-13535158.creator: Beichen Mou, Heng Tu, Jing Yang
pmc-13535158.description: Pulp canal obliteration (PCO), commonly following dental trauma, is characterized by progressive canal calcification and may be associated with pulp necrosis and apical periodontitis (AP). Conventional root canal treatment (RCT) may be technically unfeasible or associated with a high risk of iatrogenic complications.

pmc-13570276.title: The central function and specific molecular mechanisms of the TLR4 pathway underlying impaired intestinal barrier in necrotizing enterocolitis
pmc-13570276.creator: Xin Ren, Xiulan Su, Gaowa Arigong
pmc-13570276.description: Neonatal necrotizing enterocolitisis a fatal gastrointestinal emergency affecting preterm infants, which is linked to destruction of intestinal barrier. The structural overexpression and negative regulation of Toll like receptor 4, a key receptor of lipopolysaccharidefrom Gram-negative bacteria in preterm intestinal epithelial cells, constitute a core hub connecting flora dysbiosis and barrier breakdown.

pmc-13588886.title: Solvent-based post-processing to fill layer gaps in FFF-printed polypropylene fluidic chips and their application to flow injection analysis
pmc-13588886.creator: Tomohisa Yamashita
pmc-13588886.description: The development of new analytical tools remains a powerful approach in analytical chemistry, and three-dimensional (3D) printing has gained increasing popularity as a manufacturing technique in recent years. The fabrication of experimental tools using 3D printers has attracted attention in many fields.

pmc-13634916.title: MT-MRI for detection of renal interstitial fibrosis in renovascular disease
pmc-13634916.creator: YaFei Liu, Dilbar A. Abdurakhimova, Mina Al Saeedi, XiangYang Zhu, Hui Tang, Ailing Xue, Richard G. Frimpong, Sanjay Misra, Gary L. Schwartz, Amir Lerman, Aleksandra Kukla, Lilach O. Lerman
pmc-13634916.description: We evaluated kidney fibrosis in renovascular disease (RVD) using quantitative (q) and semi-quantitative magnetization-transfer (MT) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Ten RVD patients and 22 healthy volunteers (HVs) were prospectively enrolled. Of HVs, 10 (HV-1) underwent imaging studies whereas plasma samples were collected from 12 others (HV-2).

pmc-13675160.title: Mechanical ventilation–associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework
pmc-13675160.creator: Ying Gao, Yipeng Fang, Silvia De Rosa, Michele Salvagno, Lina Zhao, Keliang Xie, Fabio Silvio Taccone
pmc-13675160.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mechanical ventilation–associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung–kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid–base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation.
